desktop.notes:
• Memory cards are read gently: a folder on a card (a removable drive in Windows) is analysed 2 photos at a time instead of 6 - cards, and old card readers that do not really support today's large cards, drop out when read hard. Disks and USB SSDs keep full speed.
• A card that stops responding stops the analysis with one clear warning instead of thousands of "could not be analysed" errors: Cullect did not change any photo; don't format the card or shoot on it; safely remove it, try another reader or the camera's cable, copy the photos first (Backup & Verify); recovery tools such as PhotoRec can often get lost photos back while nothing new is written to the card. Damaged photos are not mistaken for it. (Phone: a short message.)
• Nothing more is written to a card that dropped out (the .cullect file) until its folder is opened again.
• New tests prove that opening, scanning, analysing and saving leave every photo byte-for-byte identical - the only file Cullect adds to a folder is .cullect/cullect.json.
